items.stem: In ITIL 4, value is best described as being:

options.text: Co-created through an active collaboration between provider and consumer
options.rationale: Correct: ITIL 4 holds that value is co-created, not delivered one-way by the provider.

options.text: Delivered entirely by the service provider at go-live
options.rationale: Value is co-created over the relationship, not handed over once at go-live.

options.text: Determined solely by the provider's costs
options.rationale: Value reflects consumer outcomes and perception, not just provider cost.

options.text: Fixed for the life of the contract
options.rationale: Perceived value changes as needs and context change.

items.explanation: Correct: ITIL 4 holds that value is co-created, not delivered one-way by the provider.

items.stem: Which activity is part of 'onboarding' in Drive Stakeholder Value?

options.text: Establishing user access and enabling mutual readiness to use the service
options.rationale: Correct: onboarding sets up users and raises mutual capability so value can be realised.

options.text: Decommissioning the service at end of contract
Writing the root-cause analysis of an incident
options.rationale: That is problem management, not onboarding.
That is change enablement, unrelated to onboarding.

items.explanation: Correct: onboarding sets up users and raises mutual capability so value can be realised.

items.stem: Which TWO are types of customer/provider relationship described in Drive Stakeholder Value?

options.rationale: Correct: a cooperative relationship is one of the described types.
Correct: a partnership is the most strategic described relationship type.
This is not one of the described constructive relationship types.
This is not a defined relationship type in the guidance.
Not a defined relationship type; the types are basic, cooperative and partnership.

items.explanation: Correct: a cooperative relationship is one of the described types.
